root_cause.text: In `atmel_sha204a_rng_read_nonblocking()`, a memory allocation failure for `work_data` causes the function to return `-ENOMEM` without decrementing the previously incremented `i2c_priv->tfm_count` atomic counter, leaking the count and blocking future reads.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `atomic_dec(&i2c_priv->tfm_count);` before the `return -ENOMEM;` when `kmalloc_obj` fails, explicitly fixing the missing decrement on the error path.

Author: Ard Biesheuvel <ardb@kernel.org>

    crypto: atmel-i2c - add support for SHA204A random number generator
    
    The Linaro/96boards Secure96 mezzanine contains (among other things)
    an Atmel SHA204A symmetric crypto processor. This chip implements a
    number of different functionalities, but one that is highly useful

bic_trace_step.reason: In the function `atmel_sha204a_rng_read_nonblocking`, the atomic counter `tfm_count` is incremented via `atomic_add_unless(&i2c_priv->tfm_count, 1, 1)` (line ~38). If the subsequent `kmalloc` fails (line ~50: `if (!work_data) return -ENOMEM;`), the function returns without decrementing `tfm_count`. The decrement only happens in the completion callback `atmel_sha204a_rng_done` (`atomic_dec(&i2c_priv->tfm_count)`) which is not called on allocation failure. This leaks the count, permanently preventing future reads from proceeding.
